props.text: Learn how to measure analytics limits
Real bearing recordings. Ordinary Jython tag events. Your machine, your measurements.

Click once and watch the curve build. We increase from 20 to 500 input tags, sending one burst per tag each second and testing each level for 60 seconds. The scan stops when processing falls behind or a safety limit is reached. Allow up to 15 minutes.

props.text: Below the diagonal: work accumulates or is lost. Rates exclude the first 10 seconds and the final drain, with at least 10 seconds of measurement. Use 60-second runs and the queue trace below to assess sustained overload. No point appears for runs too short to measure.

title.text: Does the waiting queue settle, or keep growing?

transforms.code: return max(10.0, max([float(row["waiting"] or 0) for row in value] or [0]) * 1.15)

props.text: Waiting = published bursts − callbacks started. After a missed event, that estimate is no longer a queue count.
Compare these charts with Docker Desktop → gateway → Stats. Raw run data is saved in your local results folder.
Each burst: 20,480 accelerometer samples (1.024 ≈ 1 s), 14 statistical indicators and 22 output updates.
The scan brackets the limit for this workload and these resources. Inspect sustained queue growth and missed events; a late publisher means the schedule itself could not keep up.
